title: vfunc.js — Keep your HTML. Control or reuse only what you need.
description: A JavaScript UI library you use with one script tag and no build step. Add behaviour to the HTML you have, or build a small SPA.

items.title: No build step
items.text: No bundler and no JSX. The code in the browser's developer tools is the code you wrote.

items.title: Works with the HTML you have
items.text: Pages from a designer stay as they are. Add behaviour only where it is needed, such as a search box or a table, with `vf.attach`.

items.title: Safe by default
items.text: `vf.html` escapes each value for where it goes. `onclick` attributes and `javascript:` addresses are blocked.

items.title: Fewer AI mistakes
items.text: A component is a plain object of `state`, `render` and `delegates`. Rules and a reference for AI tools come with it.

components.title: Components
components.lead: `vs*` returns a piece of HTML; `vf*` returns a live instance. Texts come in English and Korean; colors follow the design tokens.

items.q: Can it replace React or Vue?
items.a: For business screens, published pages, in-house systems and small SPAs, yes. For screens that update thousands of rows often, or large apps built by big teams, React or Vue may fit better.
`render` redraws the whole inside. For long lists where a few rows change often, the official `vfList` plugin draws only the changed rows. The FAQ has the measurements.

items.q: Can search engines read the pages?
items.a: The server or static files make the HTML and vfunc only adds behaviour, so search engines read that HTML as it is. This site is built that way.
Use `vfunc.legacy.min.js`. The API is the same; write the app code in ES5.
